clue.text: Limited power of the military initially disregarded

indicators.note: the opening letter is the one ignored, so the word loses its head

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
martial means relating to the military

explanation.surface: An army whose authority was curtailed because it was ignored from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited power' looks like one phrase, but the definition is the single word 'Limited'; power is only the abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something partial is incomplete or restricted in extent, just as a limited success is only part of one.

clue.text: Now, their frolicking became tiresome

indicators.note: frolicking letters skip about playfully and land in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some people's playful antics have finally grown boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke that wore thin lost its appeal through repetition and so grew tedious.

clue.text: Plant with Jennies in the middle and at the back

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

indicators.note: only the centre letter of the name is wanted

parts.note: the fourth of its seven letters

explanation.surface: A gardener positions a plant between some Jennies and behind them too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb, as in placing someone; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word for toward or at the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Intended somehow to start acquiring new sources of cash

indicators.note: the build so far takes in another letter, which ends up inside it

parts.note: one's intended is the person one is engaged to

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word before is used

parts.note: first letter of somehow
N is the usual abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone planned to begin raising fresh revenue in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' reads as a verb but is the noun for a betrothed partner; FIANCES takes in N after FI to give FINANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Finances are the monetary resources of a person or organisation, the funds they can draw on.

clue.text: Online broadcast of games might ultimately be boring?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a live internet transmission, such as of video gaming
second meaning: running water that in time wears its way through rock

explanation.surface: A gamer wonders whether a live online session of play will end up dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull; the second sense is drilling through, as running water erodes a channel over the ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook carves its bed slowly, and live internet video of gameplay is the other sense of the word.

clue.text: Normal person frequenting a local pub

explanation.surface: An ordinary person who drinks at the neighbourhood bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means usual or standard as an adjective, and as a noun a customer who keeps coming back.

clue.text: Renowned fellow — a mostly quiet sort

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is kept, so its final letter goes

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written
a timid, retiring person is called a mouse

explanation.surface: A celebrated man who is nonetheless rather shy and retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUSE loses its last letter to give MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone famous is widely known and celebrated, which is what renowned means.

clue.text: What may help you write CV on a PC?

definitions.text: What may help you write CV on a PC?

parts.words: What may help you write CV on a PC?
parts.note: surface reading: software or advice for drafting a curriculum vitae on a computer
setter's reading: typing the letters C and V as capitals needs a particular keyboard button held down

explanation.surface: A job hunter looks for help preparing a résumé on their computer.
explanation.walkthrough: CV looks like a résumé to be written; it is just two capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding this keyboard button produces upper-case letters, so typing capital C and V needs it.

clue.text: Extraordinary ruler stopping breakaway faction

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusual monarch halts a group of rebels who want to secede.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter group is a small faction that has broken off from a larger party or organisation.

clue.text: Exquisite brownstone the realtor takes on

indicators.note: the run of words takes on board the answer, holding it inside their letters

parts.note: spans the end of brownstone, all of the and the start of realtor

explanation.surface: An estate agent signs up a fine New York townhouse for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A brownstone is a type of New York terraced house; a realtor is an American estate agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes delicate, almost unearthly beauty, close to exquisite in its refinement.

clue.text: Possible route from a sports arena?

parts.note: taken as written
a stadium is a venue for sport

explanation.surface: Someone asks which way leads away from a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer also means a possible approach, as in an avenue to explore.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad street and, figuratively, a possible line of approach or way forward.

clue.text: Gambling business infiltrated by hot new exploit

indicators.note: being infiltrated means having something slip inside, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: a casino is a gambling house
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A gaming house is penetrated by a fresh hacking technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads like the hacker's noun; it is the verb. Only the hot letter goes inside; the new letter simply ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash in on a situation is to take advantage of it for profit, the verb sense of exploit.

clue.text: Butterflies seen in gardens, parks, and fields?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: orange-brown butterflies with a white comma-shaped mark on the wing

definitions.text: seen in gardens, parks, and fields
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the punctuation marks visible in that very list

explanation.surface: A wildlife note on where certain butterflies can be spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: The places named seem to be habitats, but look at the clue itself: two punctuation marks sit in that list.
explanation.definitionFit: The comma is a British butterfly species, and the clue's list literally contains two of these punctuation marks.

clue.text: Need a month off around the beginning of summer even more

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit on either side of another letter
off here means wrong or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: first letter of summer

explanation.surface: A worker pleads for a month of holiday around the start of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' sounds like time off work; it is the scramble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom and then some means plus a good deal extra, so it serves as an emphatic even more.

clue.text: Ideas that guy fed to right wing politicians

indicators.note: food goes inside whoever is fed, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party
the pronoun for a male person

explanation.surface: A man's proposals are passed to Conservative politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are speculative explanations or notions, so ideas is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Principal type of metal covering a support

parts.note: main means chief or principal

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around something, so one piece wraps the next

parts.note: tin is one kind of metal
taken as written

explanation.surface: The chief kind of metal sheathing a structural prop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' looks like a beam or brace in the surface; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain someone is to provide for and sustain them, which is to support them.

clue.text: Cattle illness resulting from rise of strange, nasty weather?

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
rain is unpleasant weather

explanation.surface: Livestock disease blamed on an odd spell of foul weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum, besides the drink, is an old British word for peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an archaic term for infectious disease in cattle, such as foot-and-mouth.

clue.text: Mallet regularly grabbed by savage sculptor

indicators.note: what is grabbed is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: gory means bloody or savage

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A wild sculptor seizes a carving hammer at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony Gormley is the British sculptor behind the Angel of the North.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony Gormley is a celebrated modern British sculptor of human figures, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Antipodean in Paris too exhausted to get going

parts.note: aussi is French for also

indicators.note: the getting going of a word is its opening, so its first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of exhausted

explanation.surface: An Australian in the French capital is also too tired to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' tells you to translate into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean refers to Australia and New Zealand, and an Aussie is an informal word for an Australian.

clue.text: Weird crap covered by national broadcaster

indicators.note: a cover goes around something, so one piece lies inside the other

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
poo is a childish word for excrement

explanation.surface: Strange rubbish reported by a nationwide TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooky means eerie or unnervingly strange, close to weird in meaning.

clue.text: Body of soldiers in Saigon manoeuvred to protect both sides of river

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the others
manoeuvred letters are moved about into new positions

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of the next word are used

parts.note: first and last letters of river

explanation.surface: Troops in the Vietnamese city deploy to guard both banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body of soldiers in Saigon' reads as one phrase; 'in' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is the troops stationed in a town or fort to defend it.

clue.text: Something used for smoking jacket

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a thick double-breasted coat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoking jacket' looks like one item of clothing; split it into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a marijuana joint and also names a short heavy coat worn by sailors.

clue.text: Fiery feeling of hatred periodically shared by us

indicators.note: at regular periods, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
what we share is ours, the possessive of us

explanation.surface: A burning loathing that flares up from time to time among us all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiery feeling of hatred' looks like one phrase; the definition stops at 'feeling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense passion or enthusiasm, a warm and burning emotion.

clue.text: Additional working hours in public institutions, maybe excessive at first

parts.note: overt means open and public

indicators.note: only the first letter of each of the preceding words is used

parts.note: initials of the three words

explanation.surface: Staff in public bodies may be putting in too many extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In public institutions' reads as one phrase; 'in' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is time worked beyond normal hours, usually paid at a higher rate.

clue.text: I'm after a lift, and this could be just the tonic!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a request to be collected by car

definitions.text: this could be just the tonic
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a reviving drink or treat

explanation.surface: Someone wanting cheering up says a boost would do them good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' means both a ride and a boost in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the words ask for a ride, and as a noun they name a restorative drink or anything that lifts one's mood.

clue.text: Left buzzing, having taken cocaine

indicators.note: having something taken away means it is removed from the word

parts.note: buzzing means thrilled and agitated
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Someone departed high on drugs after snorting cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having taken cocaine' suggests drug use; here taken means taken out, so EXCITED loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Exited is the past tense of exit, meaning went out, so it matches left as a verb.
